nominees.name: Christian J. Bordé
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire de Physique des Lasers, Université Sorbonne Paris Nord / CNRS, France

motivation: Atom interferometry turned de Broglie's matter waves into a precision tool. Bordé showed that the recoil from absorbing photons could act as a coherent beam splitter for atoms, which unified Ramsey spectroscopy and interferometry. Pritchard's group built the first atom interferometer using material diffraction gratings and used it to measure atomic polarizabilities, the index of refraction for matter waves, and decoherence. Kasevich, first with Chu, developed light-pulse interferometers with laser-cooled atoms. These now give some of the best measurements of local gravity, rotation, the fine-structure constant through photon recoil, and Newton's constant, and they underpin quantum sensors for navigation and geodesy. The field has changed what fundamental tests and practical measurements experiments can reach, and hundreds of laboratories around the world, including groups in developing countries, now practise it. It is a mature, foundational advance in quantum physics that has not yet been recognized.
